prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 3 columns and 3 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 7 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a colouring-book drawing: contours only, in one thin uniform black line on white, most of the panel left white. Draw only the people and the few large shapes of the place (walls, doors, windows, a bed, a car). People are simple storyboard figures: hair is one smooth outline of its shape, like a cap, empty inside, with no strands, curls or waves; a face has one short line each for the eyes, brows, nose and mouth, and no stubble, wrinkles or jaw lines; a fence is its posts and top rail, a tree its outline. No texture, mesh, bricks, leaves or fabric folds; no shading, grey or solid black: dark hair, clothes and cars are outlines left white inside. Thin black panel borders, plain white gutters. Location: Sebastian's apartment, living room, Day, soft bright sunlight through the floor-to-ceiling window.
Image 1: the character sheet of Natalie (25), look S3
Image 2: the character sheet of Natalie (25), look S4
Image 3: the character sheet of Sebastian (30), look S4
Image 4: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 5: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 6: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 7: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 8: the location Sebastian's apartment, living room, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Image 9: the blocking reference of this segment, the same place with its people in their places at the start; use it only for where each person is and which way they face, and keep each person on that seat or spot, on the same side of the room, in every panel until a shot moves them; do not copy its colours or light
Image 10: the prop the bag containing her wedding dress; use only structure, material, and color
Image 11: the prop two coins; use only structure, material, and color
Image 12: the prop Sebastian's phone; use only structure, material, and color
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image, by the shape of the hairstyle, the build and the outfit in outline only; never copy the photograph's detail. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Natalie stands in front of the round coffee table facing Sebastian, the dress bag over her left arm and her small nude handbag on her shoulder, in the cornflower-blue wrap dress. Sebastian stands between the charcoal couch and the round coffee table facing her, the two coins closed in his right hand. The folded blanket lies on the couch. Breakfast and Sebastian's phone, face down, are on the round dining table. The cropped ivory jacket hangs on the wall hooks beside the front door.
Panel 1: Wide shot, slow pan following Natalie from the coffee table to the front door, eye-level, from the bookshelves side. Natalie walks to the front door on the left wall, takes the cropped ivory bouclé jacket off the wall hook and pulls it on over her dress, the dress bag still on her arm; Sebastian stays by the couch watching her.
Panel 2: Medium shot, locked-off, eye-level, on the front door. Natalie, now in the open cropped jacket, opens the dark-grey front door, glances back once, steps out and the door swings shut behind her.
Panel 3: Medium shot, tracking with Sebastian from the couch to the dining table, eye-level. Sebastian walks to the round dining table and stops on its couch side, opening his hand over the table.
Panel 4: Close-up insert, high angle, locked-off, on the table top. Sebastian's fingers set the two coins down beside his face-down phone.
Panel 5: Medium close-up, low angle, slow tilt up from the table to Sebastian's face. Sebastian picks up the phone, taps it and lifts it to his ear; his lazy smile drops into a cold, focused look.
Panel 6: Close-up, locked-off, eye-level, on Sebastian's face and the phone. Sebastian speaks low into the phone, eyes fixed on the closed front door.
Panel 7: Medium shot, locked-off, eye-level, from the bookshelves side. Daniel is off screen, his voice coming from the phone. Sebastian lowers the phone from his ear and stands at the dining table.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering.
